title: Stop a wobbly stool rocking: find which corners rock, then push a shim under the right foot until snug
context: A wooden step stool with one leg 4 mm short rocks on a flat floor. A wobble is the four feet not lying in one plane: the stool rocks about one diagonal, and a shim of the right thickness under either foot of the other diagonal stops it, while a shim under one of the two feet that always bear makes it worse. Which leg is short changes with the seed, so the robot has to find the rocking corners (by pressing them, or by spotting the foot that hangs) before it pushes a wedge in just far enough.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table; front is the side facing the robot. Stool: eHemco solid hardwood step stool, one step (12.25 in tall, 12.75 x 12.75 in overall, 6.6 lb), modeled as a 28 cm square top 2.2 cm thick, four 3.2 cm square legs splayed from 23.6 cm apart (centers) under the top to 29.2 cm apart at the feet, and four 1.8 x 2 cm stretchers 9.5 cm up; 3.0 kg; part sizes estimated from maker photos. Middle at (34, 0). One leg is 4 mm short (STOOL_SEED mod 4: 0 front left, 1 back left, 2 back right, 3 front right); the stool stands level on its three long legs with the short foot 4 mm up; a press on that corner tips it onto the short foot and lifts the diagonal partner's foot. Shims: two Wobble Wedges, standard rigid (polypropylene, black), 1.92 x 1.11 in, tapering from 0.03 in to 0.25 in, each flat beside the stool at (34, +23.5) and (34, -23.5), long side along y, thin end toward the stool. Arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. Real rig: one leg sawn or sanded 4 mm short (or 4 mm craft-plywood pads under the other three), checked by a 4 mm drill shank sliding under the hanging foot and a 5 mm one not; the stool is turned so the short leg sits at the seed's corner.
scoring: Once the robot has worked on the stool (an arm or a shim within 2 cm of it) and both arms have then been at least 2 cm from the stool (every arm link against the stool's box, feet to seat) for 2 s, every shim within 2 cm of that box is let go (no fingertip within 5 mm of it) and lying on the table (tipped under 15 degrees, bottom within 2 mm; a stacked or flipped shim is not), and the stool is still (under 1 cm/s and 0.05 rad/s), the scorer presses each seat corner in turn (11.5 cm from the middle along x and y, inside the feet) straight down with 20 N for 0.5 s and records each foot's height at the end of each press; the rock is the most any foot moves between the four presses. 1.0: rock under 1 mm, the stool within 2 cm of its start and tipped under 10 degrees. 0.5: rock under 2 mm (less than half the starting 4 mm), the stool still on its marks and upright. 0.25: a shim lies flat on the table (tipped under 15 degrees, bottom within 2 mm) under at least a quarter of a foot of the rocking pair, none under the other two feet. 0: anything else (doing nothing: no presses, and pressed the rock is 4 mm; a shim under a foot that always bears; the stool moved over 2 cm or tipped; an arm back within 2 cm of the stool, which drops the result until the arms are clear and the presses repeat; presses not finished). Real trial (feeler gauges, 2 kg bag of sugar): once neither arm has touched the stool or a wedge for 2 s and both have moved back from it, and every wedge by the stool lies flat on the table (not on its side, not stacked) with the stool's feet on their tape marks (within 2 cm; otherwise 0), set the bag on each seat corner's quarter in turn (as close to the corner as it sits without hanging over) and try each foot with the 1.00 mm blade: under a foot on the table from any side; for a foot on a wedge, along the wedge's top from its thick end toward the foot (past the foot's edge the wedge's top falls away, so a gap under the rest of the foot is not a lift). 1.0 if the blade goes under no foot in any placing; 0.5 if none takes the 2.00 mm blade (or two 1.00 mm blades stacked); 0.25 if, with the bag on a rocking-pair foot's corner, a wedge under that foot stays put under a light finger-and-thumb tug and no wedge is held that way under either other foot. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Take the shim out, set the stool's feet on their tape marks, lay the shims on their marks. Under a minute. In simulation the reset is exact.
fidelity: Rigid bodies: the stool and the shims are free bodies; a shim lifts a foot only by contact and stays by friction (0.4 / 0.3, wood on wood; the shim given the same). The shim's grip ribs are not modeled. The scorer's corner presses are forces applied to the stool in the simulator, in place of the bag of sugar.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (seed 0; never reached the stool); demo: 1.0 (seed 0) and 1.0 (seed 1); variants: nothing 0, wrong-foot shim 0, arm left on the seat 0, presses without a shim 0
